dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "17 West-region annual-plan renewals were posted on 31 May, with effective dates earlier in May."
"All affected dealer-upload rows were accepted with no duplicate source-event IDs."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The month-end posting pattern is consistent with the documented upload process."
"If those checks agree, close the alert and use `effective_event_date` rather than `posted_at` for trend analysis where appropriate."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The supplied evidence does not independently verify the underlying dealer contracts or the entitlement-system audit trail."

"The decision would change if contract records showed that month-end posting was not permitted, upstream entitlement records showed duplicate renewals, or an independent reconciliation revealed a cash/ledger mismatch."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not reverse or delete the 31-May revenue."
"Perform a targeted reconciliation of the 17 affected renewals against the entitlement/source system and confirm the dealers' contract terms."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material issue."
"If those checks agree, close the alert and use `effective_event_date` rather than `posted_at` for trend analysis where appropriate."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Manipulated reporting: Rejected because the effective dates precede the 31-May posting date and the affected batches reconcile to the ledger without a financial difference." Timing and reconciliation do not independently rule out intentional manipulation of retention reporting.

"Pipeline defect: Rejected because the dealer files were accepted successfully and passed the stated control checks." Successful ingestion and source-event uniqueness do not exclude a defect in timestamp assignment, event-date handling, or downstream analytics.

"Duplicate revenue: Rejected because the affected imports passed source-event uniqueness checks and showed zero duplicate source-event IDs." Unique source-event IDs do not by themselves exclude duplicate business events represented by different IDs.

"The dealers are permitted to submit annual-renewal files monthly" is supported primarily by the dealer email; independent contract verification remains outstanding, as the submission itself acknowledges.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled duplicate revenue and a benign month-end posting process well, but it did not fully test the alternative that a pipeline or reporting defect altered event-time attribution while still passing import controls. It also treated the absence of duplicate IDs as stronger evidence against manipulation than it is.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Show a reproducible row-level reconciliation joining the 17 recharge records to entitlement and import records, including unique source_event_id counts, cash/ledger totals, effective_event_date coverage, and any duplicate entitlement IDs; use that same evidence to narrow the claims about manipulation and pipeline defects.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South-region tickets fell from 198 before the pilot to 124 after the pilot, a 37% decline."
"The containment dashboard excludes sessions ending before subscriber authentication and these are tracked outside CareDesk reporting."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The observed decline is therefore more consistent with reduced case capture/changed routing than a proven improvement in customer experience."
"NovaIVR had 507 errors and 591 abandoned sessions, so fewer CareDesk cases do not necessarily mean fewer customer problems."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "What happened to subscribers whose NovaIVR sessions ended without a CareDesk case—successful resolution, abandonment, or later contact through another channel?"
"The available interaction data does not show that sessions ending without a case were successfully resolved."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet."

"Keep the South pilot running, but do not expand nationally. Run a controlled evaluation for at least two complete weeks using successful self-service, repeat contacts, errors, abandonments, downstream complaints, and case creation as separate outcomes."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision-changing evidence: Verified self-service completion, repeat contacts by subscriber, downstream complaints/escalations, and outcomes of error/abandoned sessions."
"For sessions ending before authentication, how many subscribers later contacted CareDesk or another support channel?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The pilot sharply reduced CareDesk case creation" is directionally plausible, but the submission compares different legacy and NovaIVR session cohorts and does not provide a normalized, linked subscriber-level comparison or establish that the difference is attributable solely to the pilot.

"The decline was caused by fewer service problems: Rejected" is somewhat too definitive from service-event counts of 7 versus 9; those events are useful triangulation but are not a complete measure of customer friction.
The recommendation to evaluate "at least two complete weeks" is operationally specific but the duration is not justified by the cited evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative—that sessions without CareDesk cases may represent successful self-service rather than failed capture—by preserving it as an unknown and requesting verified completion, sampled sessions, and downstream outcomes. It did not fully explore broader benign explanations such as seasonality or differences in exposure between legacy and NovaIVR cohorts.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Link NovaIVR sessions to subscriber-level downstream contacts and journey outcomes, with a defined successful-resolution event and sampled call/session review, so case suppression can be distinguished from genuine resolution.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies `inverter_events.csv` and specific fields: “All 4 events have `impact_mw = 0` and `cleared = yes`.”
It also cites event IDs, classifications, durations, and impact fields rather than relying only on the brief.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The analyst cross-checks several event attributes: “no inverter repeats, all events are cleared, all report zero MW impact, and none is classified as a critical/failure event.”
The reasoning is appropriately bounded, but it relies primarily on one event file and does not independently verify the operational telemetry or the semantics of the impact field.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission distinguishes confidence levels, assigning high confidence to file observations and medium confidence to the validation need.
It explicitly limits the conclusion: “The supplied file alone does not justify escalation or an inference of equipment failure, intent, or commercial impact.”

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation is proportionate and discriminating: “Perform one cheap check, then stop if it passes.”
The proposed check directly tests the main residual uncertainty: whether `impact_mw = 0` is correctly populated for these event types.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly avoids inventing a plant problem from short, cleared events with zero reported MW impact.
It preserves a limited quality-control check while rejecting unsupported escalation or causal claims.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The only item worth a cheap check” is a prioritization judgment rather than a fully demonstrated conclusion; other data-quality or timing checks could also be reasonable, though none appears decision-changing from the supplied evidence.

“No direct evidence of material equipment impact” is appropriately scoped, but zero impact remains an observed file value rather than independently verified telemetry; the analyst acknowledges this limitation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The events could represent transient communications or status warnings with no plant impact, but the repeated zero value could also be a default or incorrectly populated field. That data-quality explanation is the strongest alternative requiring a cheap check before stopping.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State exactly how to validate `impact_mw`: compare the event records with the field definition and contemporaneous inverter/SCADA generation or power telemetry for the four event windows. If the zero semantics are confirmed, stop rather than pursue a broader failure narrative.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites "dispatch_blocks.csv; Impact Note" for the 31.6% and 25.4% figures, but does not identify the relevant records, fields, or calculations.
The statement that DSM settlement depends on "accepted schedule, meter data and deviation bands" is traceable to "DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf".
The central statement that the data does not identify the counterfactual overlooks the supplied base_schedule_mw and submitted_schedule_mw fields for 29 May.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly notes that "only one conventional day and one AI-assisted day are compared" and that weather and operating conditions could differ.
It does not perform or describe the available same-day comparison between base_schedule_mw and submitted_schedule_mw on 29 May.
Weather and generation conditions are listed as possible explanations, but no independent channel or data-based test is used to assess them.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The distinction between "31.6% lower observed DSM penalty" and proof that "the AI-assisted pilot caused the reduction" is appropriately calibrated.
The submission explicitly labels the causal claim "Low" and recommends collecting multiple events before causal attribution.
Its claim that the data cannot identify the counterfactual is too broad because an operational same-day counterfactual is available, even though it is not a fully controlled causal estimate.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to "continue the pilot during high-wind conditions" while not treating 31.6% as proven causal savings is proportionate to the evidence.
The proposed next measurement—recording both the AI-assisted recommendation and the conventional/base schedule under matched conditions—is directionally useful.
It is less discriminating than immediately analyzing the already available 29 May base-versus-submitted schedules and does not specify the outcome or acceptance criteria for expansion.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly preserves the distinction between a favorable pilot-day observation and a causal claim about 31.6%.
It correctly recognizes the different-day comparison as a causal limitation.

It misses the smaller same-day benefit available from comparing base_schedule_mw with submitted_schedule_mw on 29 May, so it under-scopes the evidence by implying that no pilot effect can be estimated at all.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The data does not identify the counterfactual" is overstated: the supplied 29 May base_schedule_mw and submitted_schedule_mw provide an operational same-day counterfactual, although not a fully controlled causal estimate.
The submission presents the 31.6% and 25.4% figures as reproducible/high-confidence without showing the underlying block-level calculation or identifying the relevant fields and dates.
The listed alternative explanations—weather, generation conditions, and operating factors—are plausible but are not actually tested or rejected with evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot-day result is not limited to an uncontrolled 31.6% cross-day comparison. Comparing submitted_schedule_mw with base_schedule_mw on 29 May provides evidence of a smaller same-day improvement, supporting some operational value while still not proving that the pilot caused the full 31.6% reduction.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Analyze and report the 29 May base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw comparison, including the resulting DSM penalty and generation gap, before relying on future events for the causal assessment.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "P1001 is declared under tariff code 90211000 with US origin." — Source: "declaration.pdf"
"P1001 is listed as 90211000 in the Swiss tariff matrix." — Source: "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx"
"P1001 has Helios commodity code 90211090 in the product master." — Source: "product_master_current.xlsx"
"The AWB links shipment SHP-000522 to declaration CH-2025-000522 and Switzerland." — Source: "air_waybill.pdf"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Declaration error: Rejected because the declared 90211000 agrees with the Swiss tariff reference."
"Wrong product classification caused by product mismatch: Rejected because P1001 and the Titanium acetabular cup description are consistent across the declaration and invoice."

"Automated flag is sufficient proof of an error: Rejected because it compares the Helios code with the Swiss declaration code without establishing that both codes use the same jurisdiction-specific nomenclature."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Do not escalate as a likely declaration error."
"The Swiss tariff matrix supports 90211000 for P1001, so the automated mismatch is not sufficient evidence of an incorrect declaration."
"A Swiss Tares classification or product-specific customs ruling for P1001 would provide the strongest independent confirmation."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The mismatch is explained by the use of different tariff-code systems: the declaration uses Swiss code 90211000, while the product master lists Helios code 90211090."
"It compares the Helios code with the Swiss declaration code without establishing that both codes use the same jurisdiction-specific nomenclature."
"Update the mismatch rule to distinguish Helios and Swiss tariff-code systems."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not amend the declaration solely because of the automated flag."
"Perform one targeted check against the applicable Swiss tariff/Tares classification or ruling for P1001."
"If it confirms 90211000, close the alert as a false positive and update the mismatch rule."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The Swiss tariff matrix supports 90211000 for P1001" is stated at high confidence but is not tied to a worksheet, row, or cell, and the submission does not explain whether the matrix is authoritative for the specific product classification.

"Declaration error: Rejected" is somewhat stronger than the evidence warrants because the cited matrix agreement reduces the likelihood of error but does not independently establish that the product-specific Swiss classification is correct.

The evidence table labels several claims "High" confidence without describing source limitations or confirming that the product master, declaration, invoice, and tariff matrix share the same product-identification basis.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The mismatch could still reflect an incorrect Swiss classification or an outdated/misapplied tariff-matrix entry rather than only a benign Helios-versus-Swiss code-system difference; a product-specific Swiss Tares ruling or classification review is needed to distinguish these possibilities.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Cite the exact rows or cells in the declaration, product master, invoice, and Swiss tariff matrix, and explain why the matrix entry is authoritative for P1001 before assigning high confidence or rejecting the declaration-error hypothesis.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "IE-2025-000411 claims preference \"Yes\" and declares P1006 origin as United States."
"No current supplier-origin document reference was found for SUP-02/P1006 on 2025-09-18."
"supplier_declaration_reference.txt; supplier_origin_register.csv"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Preference claim is supported simply because the declaration says \"Yes\": Rejected."
"US manufacturing origin proves preferential origin: Rejected."
"No register entry proves no supplier declaration exists: Rejected."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Do not treat the Irish preferential-origin claim as supported by the current evidence."
"this does not prove that no document exists outside the register."
"could materially change the decision."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Evidence from the supplier category folder should also be checked because the workshop notes say the register may not always be updated."
"the supplier declaration and the rule used for the claim are needed to clear a preference claim."
"the specific preference rule used by the broker"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Keep the preference claim on hold for review"
"do not clear it as supported until the supplier declaration and applicable origin rule are verified."
"Request the smallest missing evidence"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission labels the cited facts with "High" confidence but does not quote exact fields, rows, page numbers, or passages from the underlying files, so the source verification is less granular than it could be.

The statement that the AWB "confirms" the shipment linkage is plausible and specifically sourced, but the submission does not provide the AWB identifiers or an exact excerpt to independently verify that linkage.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: P1006 may genuinely qualify for preferential origin under the applicable rule, and the supplier declaration may exist in the supplier category folder even though the central register is stale; therefore the current evidence supports withholding clearance pending verification, not rejecting the claim or alleging fraud.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add exact excerpts, identifiers, rows, or page references from each cited source and obtain the supplier declaration together with the precise preference rule and shipment/date coverage before reaching an operational or compliance conclusion.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Many released batches have qcore_release_ts exactly at 02:10" — cites batch_release.csv and identifies the relevant field, but gives no count or row-level examples.
"LabTrack snapshot is from 29 Jul 23:00 while QCore is from 31 Jul 02:10" — cites source_freshness.csv with specific timestamps.
"The SOP defines the routine target as 24 hours from required evidence being available to disposition" — directly ties the conclusion to the governing SOP.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The observed receipt-to-release times may reflect snapshot/batch timing rather than the actual authorized disposition time" — separates a measurement mechanism from the apparent KPI symptom.

"The smallest useful check is to validate the timestamp definitions and compare a small sample with the live/source-system event times" — proposes a discriminating test rather than asserting the cause as proven.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: Uses claim-specific confidence levels in the evidence table and appropriately says timestamps "may reflect" snapshot/batch timing.
"Verify before using the apparent cycle time as a KPI" — makes source freshness and timestamp semantics decision-relevant, although it does not quantify the size of the possible distortion.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "The smallest useful check is to validate the timestamp definitions and compare a small sample with the live/source-system event times" — recommends a focused, reversible validation before dashboarding.

"If 02:10 is only a snapshot/batch timestamp, the KPI definition must be changed before dashboarding" — appropriately reframes the problem from performance management to metric validity, though explicit success criteria are limited.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The apparent cycle time is simply the true QC performance. Rejected." — tests the straightforward interpretation against the 02:10 clustering and differing refresh cadences.
"Every released batch should be judged against the 24-hour routine target. Rejected." — uses SOP exclusions and exception fields to reject blanket application of the target.
The submission does not fully articulate what evidence would revive the strongest alternative explanation beyond the general reconciliation proposed.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A data-catalog definition confirming that qcore_release_ts is the actual authorized disposition timestamp, plus a small sample reconciled to the live QCore and LabTrack event history" — requests narrowly targeted evidence that directly discriminates timestamp semantics and snapshot effects.
"would make the cycle-time KPI defensible" / "the KPI definition must be changed before dashboarding" — clearly links the evidence to the decision.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The assertion that confirming qcore_release_ts as the authorized disposition timestamp would by itself make the KPI defensible is somewhat overstated; the required-evidence-available timestamp and temporal consistency of the joined sources would also need validation.

"Many" qcore_release_ts values occur at 02:10 is plausible and relevant, but the submission provides no count, proportion, or row-level examples. It should remain an observed pattern rather than a quantified conclusion.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: 02:10 may be a legitimate, consistently batched authorized-release process rather than a reporting artifact; the timestamp definition and reconciliation to source-system event history are needed to distinguish that explanation from interface or snapshot timing.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide the count and proportion of records at 02:10, then reconcile a deliberately selected sample—including routine and exception cases—to the QCore authorization event, the required-evidence-available event, and the LabTrack source timestamps from a coherent point-in-time extract.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Several requests have exact manufacturer part number, revision and UOM matches"; sources cited as `part_requests.csv`; `spare_parts.csv`.
"Some matching stock is reserved for safety-critical assets"; sources cited as `part_restrictions.csv`; `maintenance_email.txt`.
The submission cites relevant files but does not provide row IDs, fields, quantities, dates, or a reproducible calculation for the 16.9%/54.3%/28.8% split.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Description similarity can identify candidates, but technical equivalence, revision, configuration and qualification still require confirmation."
"Every exact MPN match is transferable: Rejected. Some matching parts are reserved for critical assets."
"Global available quantity equals free stock: Rejected. The maintenance email states that global availability can lag local reservations."
The reasoning separates semantic retrieval from transferability and tests several plausible alternatives, but does not show the underlying joins or quantify how each constraint changes the result.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Of the apparent purchase value, 16.9% is actionable now, 54.3% needs an engineering check, and 28.8% is not transferable from the current evidence."
"Upstream source snapshots are not all equally current, so stock availability should be validated before acting."

The submission acknowledges stale data and uses confidence labels, but the precise percentages and several "Actionable now" classifications are not bounded by source age, quantity, reservation, or freshness-specific uncertainty.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Proceed with the semantic-search pilot, but use it only to generate candidate matches rather than automatic transfer recommendations."
"Manufacturer part number, revision, UOM, qualification, reservation status, and current free stock must be confirmed before transfer."
"The next step should be a live-stock and engineering validation of the candidate matches."
This is a useful and appropriately safeguarded reframing, though it would be stronger with a small pilot design, explicit success criteria, and a prioritized validation queue.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Similar descriptions mean the parts are interchangeable: Rejected."
"Every exact MPN match is transferable: Rejected."
"All apparent purchase value is avoidable: Rejected."

The submission actively rejects multiple strong competing explanations and identifies evidence that would revive them, although the tests are described narratively rather than demonstrated with row-level results.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "current local/CMMS data showed that apparently free stock is actually reserved or unavailable"
"Engineering confirmed or rejected equivalence for the description-only matches"
"The next step should be a live-stock and engineering validation of the candidate matches"
The requested evidence is relevant and decision-linked, but it is not prioritized into the smallest highest-value query or tied to expected changes in the recommendation.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The exact value split of 16.9% actionable, 54.3% needing engineering review, and 28.8% not transferable is not reproducibly supported because no calculation, denominators, row-level mapping, or treatment of stale snapshots is shown.

Several items labeled "Actionable now" appear to retain unresolved receiving-site, engineering, qualification, reservation, or freshness checks; the submission's own caveats therefore do not fully support that label.

"Global available quantity can lag local reservation status" is cited as a general rule, but the submission does not identify which specific candidate rows are affected or how their classifications were adjusted.
The blanket high-confidence assessments are stronger than the presented evidence trail, especially where source freshness and current free stock are decision-critical.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic-search pilot is still justified, but the apparent savings may be materially lower than stated because exact identity matches are only candidate matches and the available extracts may not be temporally coherent. The 16.9% actionable figure could therefore be a retrieval estimate rather than currently actionable value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible row-level reconciliation for every open request: exact MPN/revision/UOM and qualification checks, requested versus genuinely free quantity, reservation/criticality status, source freshness date, and the calculation producing each value bucket; then rerun it against live inventory before calling any item actionable.
